To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the calcium-independent receptor (CIRL1) is a high affinity α-LTX receptor that mediates Ca2+-permeable channels, and (2) α-LTX receptors facilitate channel formation by α-LTX.
α-latroxin binding to CIRL1, a putative GPCR, stimulates secretion from PC12 and chromaffin cells and produces high conductance channels that permit increases in cytosol Ca2+.
α-latrotoxins bind to the calcium-independent α-latrotoxic receptor, CIRL- 1, to produce channels in chromaffin and non-neuronal cells, and that channel formation is not transduced by G-proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of α-latroxin, a toxin that causes the release of neurotransmitter from presynaptic neurons.
the molecular mechanism of action of α-latrototoxin.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction of α-Latrotoxins with their receptor(s) in order to understand how this protein toxin causes neurotransmitter secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α-latroxin binds to a G-protein-couple receptor and that the G-protein-couples receptor is a calcium independent receptor (CIRL).
the interaction between α-latrotoxins and their receptors results in the formation of a channel that is controlled by the toxin itself.
α-latroxin binding to the CIRL-α-latrotoxin binding site on the CIRL receptor induces the formation of a pore, which is stabilized by α-latroxin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α-latrotoxins bind to the cell membrane and induce the formation of channels in it.

the α-latrotoxins, which are members of a family of pore-forming proteins, are capable of interacting with a variety of cell surface receptors and that these interactions can result in the formation of channels with different conductances and different Ca2+ sensitivities.
α-latroxin binding to CIRL1 and Neurexin-1α facilitates toxin induced channel formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the α-latrotoxins are not the only proteins capable of forming channels in membranes.
α-LT interaction with the calcium-independent receptor (CIRL) or with neurexin (Nx) 1α produces channels with nearly identical properties.
α-latroxin receptors are not involved in channel formation.
